draft.title: Soundtrack and silence
card: A soundtrack is the music and sound that plays under a film or show. It can tell the audience how to feel before a character says a word.
Slow, soft music can make a scene feel sad or calm. Fast, loud music with a pounding beat can build excitement or fear.
Silence is a choice too. When the sound suddenly cuts out, the audience can feel shock or tension.
Filmmakers often use a quiet moment before a loud one. The contrast makes the loud sound hit harder.
draft.remember: Music guides feelings. A sudden silence can make a moment shocking or tense.

a.q: In a short film, a girl waits at a bus stop while cheerful music plays. The music stops dead as a dark car pulls up. What effect does the silence most likely have?
opts: It creates tension and warns that something is wrong
It shows that the girl feels calm and safe
It tells the audience the scene is over
It shows that the film has run out of music
a.why: A sudden silence after cheerful music makes the audience uneasy, so it builds tension. It does not signal calm, because the change from sound to quiet is what unsettles the audience.
a.clue: Think about how you feel when a noise suddenly stops.

b.q: A film shows a boy walking alone through an empty school at night. Slow, low notes play and get faster and louder as he nears a door. What is the soundtrack most likely signalling?
opts: A funny moment about to happen
b.why: Low notes that speed up and grow louder build fear and suspense as the boy nears the door. Sadness would usually be shown with slow, soft music that does not build.
b.clue: Ask what faster, louder music does to an audience's feelings.

a.best: It creates tension and warns that something is wrong
